why: I checked each verifier check's PASS and FAIL conditions against the words of its expect line, and the criterion holds. Check 1 tests only that padLeft is exported, pads on the left to width, uses a space when fill is omitted, and takes (s, width, fill). The sample values ("00042", "  ab", "**x") just apply those words. Check 2 tests only that s comes back unchanged when it is exactly width long or longer. Check 3 asks for a section per exported function, meaning "a heading that names the function, followed by text describing it". That is a fair reading of "section" rather than an extra rule. Check 4 asks only that npm test succeeds. The stricter items are all under "Advisory (not pass or fail conditions)": test coverage of padLeft, the `## name(args)` heading style, and how a multi-character fill behaves. No mutation test, branch rule or exact-wording rule appears in any PASS or FAIL condition.
